transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hello. I get this overwhelming, out-of-proportion fear whenever I even think about driving over certain bridges or high stretches of road. It's gotten to the point where I knew I needed to seek some help.
Do you feel this fear only in those specific situations, or do you also get similar fear in other places like crowded rooms, public transportation, or being away from home?

No, it's really just limited to those bridges, overpasses, and high stretches of road. I don't have any issues with crowded rooms, public transit, or being away from home. It is very specifically tied to those elevated roadways.

When you are on or approaching those bridges or high roads, do you worry mainly about something bad happening there, like falling or losing control, rather than being judged by other people or having a panic attack?

Yes, exactly. I get this huge, sick fear that my car is just going to slide right off the edge, even though I know in my head that's not realistic and everyone else drives over them just fine. It's not about being judged by others at all—it's just that terrifying feeling of going over the side.
Do you also have this intense fear in other situations involving heights, such as looking down from tall buildings, standing on balconies, or using ladders?
No, I don't think I have that same fear with things like balconies or ladders. It really seems to be limited to just driving on those bridges and high stretches of road.
Do you have this same intense fear in other situations involving heights, such as standing on a balcony, looking down from a tall building, or using a ladder?

No, I don't really experience that kind of intense fear with balconies, tall buildings, or ladders. The fear is very specifically tied to driving over bridges, overpasses, or those high stretches of road.
When you are afraid on those bridges or high roads, is the fear mainly about the height itself, or is it more about being in a situation where you might be trapped or unable to escape?

It's not about being trapped at all. It's really just this overwhelming fear that my car is going to slide right off the edge of the road, just like the car I saw hanging off the guardrail in that bad accident.

Have you ever had a similar intense fear in other situations where there is no height involved, such as seeing a car accident, being in traffic, or thinking about bridges because of a past traumatic event?

No, I don't get that intense fear in normal traffic or other situations where there is no height involved. It really is strictly tied to those high, narrow bridges and overpasses where I feel like my car could slide off. Normal driving or seeing an accident on a flat road doesn't trigger this overwhelming panic at all.

Do you ever feel this same fear in other situations involving heights, like standing on a balcony, looking down from a tall building, or using a ladder? Or is it only when driving on bridges or high roads?

No, it is strictly when I am driving on those bridges and high roads. I don't feel this way at all on balconies, in tall buildings, or on ladders. It's really just the specific fear of my car sliding off those elevated roadways.
Do you also feel this fear in other situations where you are being driven or traveling, such as in a car, bus, train, or airplane, or is it only when you are driving on bridges and high roads?

No, I don't fear general travel like trains or airplanes at all. It is strictly tied to bridges and high roads, even if my husband is the one driving me. While having him drive helps me cope, I still get very anxious if our route involves crossing one of those bridges.
Do you also avoid or fear other specific objects or situations, like animals, injections, blood, or enclosed spaces, or is it only bridges and high roads?

No, I don't have any unusual fears or avoidance of things like animals, blood, injections, or enclosed spaces. This intense fear is strictly limited to bridges and high stretches of road. Everything else is completely fine for me.
Do you avoid these bridges or high roads so much that it interferes with your daily life, like changing your route, missing appointments, or refusing trips?

Yes, it has a huge impact on my life, and I will drive 20 minutes out of my way on back roads just to avoid a bridge. I've had to skip my church quilting group, turn down helping with food-pantry deliveries, and now rely much more on my husband to drive me because my world has gotten so much smaller.
How long have you had this fear and avoidance of bridges or high roads? Has it been present for at least 6 months?

Yes, it has been going on for much longer than six months. This all started a little over two years ago right after I witnessed that terrible accident on the bridge, and the fear has just stayed with me and even gotten worse since then.

Since the accident you witnessed, do you have unwanted memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or strong distress when reminded of it, such as avoiding thoughts about the crash or feeling constantly on edge?

No, I don't really experience nightmares, flashbacks, or feel constantly on edge like that. My distress is really just focused on the fear of driving over those bridges and high roads, rather than constantly reliving the accident itself.
Do you feel this same intense fear in many different situations that involve heights, or is it only when you are driving over bridges and high roads?

No, it isn't heights in general at all, as I am completely fine in tall buildings. It is strictly tied to driving or riding over bridges, overpasses, and high, narrow stretches of road. My fear is specifically that the car will slide off the edge or I will lose control on those structures, which connects back to that terrible accident I witnessed.
When you are on those bridges or high roads, is your fear mainly of the height itself, or is it more about the car sliding off, losing control, or another specific danger?

It is definitely about the car sliding right off the edge rather than just the height itself. This fear stems from seeing that car hanging halfway off the bridge in the fog, even though I logically know it's not realistic and everyone else drives over them just fine.
Do you fear heights in general, such as standing on a balcony, looking down from a tall building, or using a ladder, or is the fear only when driving or riding over bridges and high roads?

No, I don't fear heights in general at all. I can stand on a balcony or look out of a tall building without any issue. The fear is strictly limited to driving or riding over bridges and high roads, where I get terrified that the car is going to slide right off the edge.
When you are on those bridges or high roads, is the fear mainly about being at a height, or is it more about the possibility that your car could slip, slide, or lose control?

It is definitely about the car slipping or sliding off the edge. Ever since I saw that car hanging halfway off the bridge, I get this sick feeling that my own car will just slide right off, even though I know intellectually that it isn't realistic.

Does this fear happen only when you are driving or riding over bridges and high roads, or do you also feel it in other situations where a vehicle could slip or lose control, such as steep mountain roads, icy roads, or sharp curves?

No, I don't really worry about things like icy roads or sharp curves in general. The fear is strictly focused on bridges, overpasses, and elevated or narrow stretches of road where there is a drop-off. It's really the combination of the height and that specific, terrifying thought of sliding off the edge of an elevated structure.
Do you fear heights in general, like standing on a balcony or looking out from a tall building, or is the fear only when driving or riding over bridges and elevated roads?

No, I don't have a general fear of heights like being on a balcony or inside a tall building. The fear is strictly tied to driving or riding over bridges and elevated, narrow roadways. It is completely about the terrifying thought of my car losing control and sliding right off the edge.

Do you ever feel this same fear in other situations where a vehicle could slip or lose control, such as icy roads, steep mountain roads, or sharp curves, or is it only on bridges and elevated roadways?

No, I don't feel that panic on icy or curvy roads. I might have normal caution in those situations, but it doesn't trigger the same intense, heart-pounding terror that I get on bridges and elevated roads. That overwhelming fear is strictly tied to those high stretches of road.
Did this fear begin only after the bridge accident you witnessed, or did you have a similar fear of bridges or heights before that event?

No, I never had any fear of bridges or heights before that accident. It only started after I witnessed that awful crash on the bridge about two and a half years ago. Before then, I drove normally to my walks, errands, and quilting group without any issues at all.
Since witnessing the bridge accident, do you have unwanted memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or strong distress when reminded of it, or is the fear only about driving over bridges and high roads?

No, I don't have nightmares or flashbacks about the accident itself. While seeing reminders like a picture of that bridge or a GPS route triggers immediate, heart-pounding anxiety, the core fear is strictly about driving on those elevated structures and worrying my car will slide off.
Do you have any unwanted memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or feel constantly on edge because of the bridge accident, or is the fear only when you are actually driving over bridges or high roads?

No, I don't experience nightmares, flashbacks, or a constant feeling of being on edge. My intense fear, pounding heart, and sweaty hands are specifically triggered when I have to drive over bridges, see pictures of them, or realize a route is taking me toward an overpass. Otherwise, I don't have those kinds of distressing symptoms.
When you think about or encounter a bridge, is your fear mainly about the height and the possibility of falling, or is it more about a specific traumatic memory of the accident you witnessed?

While the fear originally started after witnessing that terrible accident with the car hanging off the bridge, the fear I experience now is really focused on the height of the structure itself. I just get this overwhelming, unrealistic feeling that my own car is going to slide right off the edge.
Do you have this same fear in other situations where you are high up but not in a car, such as standing on a balcony, looking out from a tall building, or using a ladder?
No, I don't really experience that fear in other height situations like balconies or ladders. My fear is very specifically tied to driving or being in a car on bridges and high stretches of road.
Do you also get this fear in other situations where you are high up but not in a car, such as standing on a balcony, looking out from a tall building, or using a ladder?

No, I don't experience that fear in other high places like balconies, tall buildings, or ladders. The anxiety is very specifically tied to driving or being in a car on bridges and high stretches of road.
When you are on a bridge or high road, is the fear mainly about the height itself, or more about being trapped or unable to get off the bridge until you reach the other side?

It's not about feeling trapped or unable to get off the bridge. My fear is almost entirely about the car sliding right off the edge of the road, just like the car I saw in the accident. It's that specific danger of going over the side that terrifies me.
Do you ever have unwanted memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or feel constantly on edge because of the bridge accident, or is the fear only when you are actually driving over bridges or high roads?

No, I don't experience any nightmares, flashbacks, or a constant feeling of being on edge. My fear, along with physical symptoms like my heart pounding and sweaty hands, is strictly triggered by bridges, high roads, or things that remind me of them, like seeing a bridge on the news or realizing my GPS is routing me toward an overpass.
Since the bridge accident, do you have unwanted memories, nightmares, flashbacks, or feel constantly on edge because of it, even when you are not near a bridge?

No, I don't experience any nightmares, flashbacks, or a constant feeling of being on edge when I am away from bridges. My intense fear and physical symptoms only kick in when I am actually facing, thinking about, or approaching a bridge or high road.
